cases.explain: «предстоящего сражения» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: The narrow room, in which they were smoking and taking refreshments, was full of noblemen. The excitement grew more intense, and every face betrayed some uneasiness. The excitement was specially keen for the leaders of each party, who knew every detail, and had reckoned up every vote. They were the generals organizing the approaching battle. The rest, like the rank and file before an engagement, though they were getting ready for the fight, sought for other distractions in the interval. Some were lunching, standing at the bar, or sitting at the table; others were walking up and down the long room, smoking cigarettes, and talking with friends whom they had not seen for a long while.

cases.sentence: Одни закусывали, стоя или присев к столу; другие ходили, куря папиросы, взад и вперед по ___ и разговаривали с давно не виденными приятелями.
cases.explain: «длинной комнате» — after the preposition «по», the dative marks the indirect object or recipient.
cases.translation: The narrow room, in which they were smoking and taking refreshments, was full of noblemen. The excitement grew more intense, and every face betrayed some uneasiness. The excitement was specially keen for the leaders of each party, who knew every detail, and had reckoned up every vote. They were the generals organizing the approaching battle. The rest, like the rank and file before an engagement, though they were getting ready for the fight, sought for other distractions in the interval. Some were lunching, standing at the bar, or sitting at the table; others were walking up and down the long room, smoking cigarettes, and talking with friends whom they had not seen for a long while.

cases.sentence: И помещик, кинув ___ на Левина, круто повернулся.
cases.explain: «недовольный взгляд» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: “He’s such a blackguard! I have told him so, but it makes no difference. Only think of it! He couldn’t collect it in three years!” he heard vigorously uttered by a round-shouldered, short, country gentleman, who had pomaded hair hanging on his embroidered collar, and new boots obviously put on for the occasion, with heels that tapped energetically as he spoke. Casting a displeased glance at Levin, this gentleman sharply turned his back.

cases.sentence: – Да, нечистое дело, что и говорить, – проговорил тоненьким голосом ___.
cases.explain: «маленький помещик» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Yes, it’s a dirty business, there’s no denying,” a small gentleman assented in a high voice.

cases.sentence: Вслед за этими ___ помещиков, окружавшая толстого генерала, поспешно приблизилась к Левину.
cases.explain: «целая толпа» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: Next, a whole crowd of country gentlemen, surrounding a stout general, hurriedly came near Levin. These persons were unmistakably seeking a place where they could talk without being overheard.

cases.sentence: Они на статье основываются, – говорили в ___, – жена должна быть записана дворянкой.
cases.explain: «другой группе» — after the preposition «в», for location or topic.
cases.translation: “But excuse me! They take their stand on the act,” was being said in another group; “the wife must be registered as noble.”

cases.explain: «благородные дворяне» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Oh, damn your acts! I speak from my heart. We’re all gentlemen, aren’t we? Above suspicion.”

cases.sentence: – Я Марье Семеновне всегда советовал сдать в аренду, потому что она не выгадает, – ___ говорил помещик с седыми усами, в полковничьем мундире старого генерального штаба.
cases.explain: «приятным голосом» — the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: “I always advised Marya Semyonovna to let for a fair rent, for she can never save a profit,” he heard a pleasant voice say. The speaker was a country gentleman with gray whiskers, wearing the regimental uniform of an old general staff-officer. It was the very landowner Levin had met at Sviazhsky’s. He knew him at once. The landowner too stared at Levin, and they exchanged greetings.

cases.sentence: – Я должен вам признаться, что я очень плохо понимаю значение ___, – сказал Левин.
cases.explain: «дворянских выборов» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: “I ought to own that I don’t very well understand the drift of the provincial elections,” said Levin.

cases.sentence: Посмотрите, мундиры – и эти говорят вам: – это собрание ___, непременных членов и так далее, а не дворян.
cases.explain: «мировых судей» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: “Why, what is there to understand? There’s no meaning in it at all. It’s a decaying institution that goes on running only by the force of inertia. Just look, the very uniforms tell you that it’s an assembly of justices of the peace, permanent members of the court, and so on, but not of noblemen.”
